**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Accept launcher-valid underscores in profile names**

When a model profile contains an underscore, the existing generator accepts it (`scripts/generate-agent-configs.py:77`) and `herdr-agents` accepts it and embeds it in the worker identity (`home/dot_local/bin/common/executable_herdr-agents:1818-1820,329`), but this regex rejects that identity before reading its rendered profile. Thus a valid seat such as `claude-my_profile-dot-a001` is permanently reported as `args=unknown-identity` even when its process arguments match; extend the identity parser to support the same profile-name grammar as the launcher.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

items.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Run the process probe outside the agent sandbox**

When this boundary check runs from the normal Claude orchestrator context, this subprocess inherits the agent sandbox: `home/dot_agents/skills/agmsg-orchestration/SKILL.md:56` documents that macOS Seatbelt denies `ps` and Linux bubblewrap hides outside processes. Consequently, `seat-args.sh` receives no visible worker rows and reports a healthy seat as `process=none args=unlaunched`; an executable-but-denied `ps` also reproduces this because its failure is discarded by the process substitution. Invoke the probe through an established outside-sandbox mechanism or another process source visible from the sandbox. The process-input threat-table row only describes the probes as read-only/test-replaceable and therefore does not mitigate this runtime limitation.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L75-L78](https://github.com/mryfmo/dotfiles/blob/bfae75c14f52ff1b8083a69179bd90e91aa99458/AGENTS.md#L75-L78)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

items.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Continue past uninspectable unrelated Codex processes**

When the global `ps` output contains any Codex-looking process whose cwd cannot be inspected—for example, an unrelated process owned by another user or one that exits between `ps` and `lsof`—this branch immediately returns `unknown-probe` (exit 4). `check-regime-boundary.sh` silently skips exit 4, so a later live worker process is never examined and mismatched launch arguments go unreported; continue scanning and only return unknown when no matching process can be established after accounting for failed lookups. This also leaves the process-input residual control ineffective for this availability failure mode.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L78-L78](https://github.com/mryfmo/dotfiles/blob/a428eb5ff31dc8452e22fbea332efa2a5ee9a5e8/AGENTS.md#L78-L78)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

items.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject conflicting duplicate profile flags**

When a process contains each expected pair plus a conflicting duplicate—such as `--model expected --effort xhigh --model wrong`—this loop reports `args=ok` because it only checks that the expected pairs occur somewhere. Such a process does not match the rendered launch configuration and may run under the later override, so the boundary check should reject duplicate managed flags with unexpected values; the closed threat-table case currently has no test for this scenario.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L78-L78](https://github.com/mryfmo/dotfiles/blob/1086570f8a8b20271ba7d7417701e1dff922e149/AGENTS.md#L78-L78)

items.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Redact unrelated worker arguments from diagnostics**

When a selected process has mismatched profile arguments, this prints its complete remaining command line. Codex prompts are passed as positional argv elsewhere in the repository (for example `scripts/orchestrator/codex-review.sh:37`), so a mismatched or mistakenly selected Codex process in the worker cwd can expose the full prompt—and potentially embedded credentials or private task data—in boundary output that may be retained as validation evidence; report only the managed flags needed to explain the mismatch.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L72-L72](https://github.com/mryfmo/dotfiles/blob/1086570f8a8b20271ba7d7417701e1dff922e149/AGENTS.md#L72-L72)
